notes.title: Disco Elysium s Hardcore Mode is just one way games can meaningfully explore poverty
notes.content:
Last week, the haunting and hilarious Disco Elysium added an extra difficulty setting called Hardcore True Detective Mode . On the surface, it seems like a fairly standard set of tweaked parameters. More demanding dice roles to shaft dear old Harry Du Bois at every opportunity.

If you take time to read the update notes though, it becomes clear that these new changes are storytelling devices as much as adjusted sliders. Since there are no monsters to make tougher, it s your wallet and psyche that take the hits. It s had me thinking about how ZA/UM s surrealist cop odyssey, and other games, express poverty through their systems. Games that invert the traditional power curve of farmhand to godhood, or make us try twice as hard to get half as far. Far from being a detached add-on, the update is a deft application of mechanics-as-metaphor that wouldn t work if desperation, isolation, poverty, and addiction weren t already stitched deep into the fabric of Disco Elysium s fiction.

(more…)

notes.title: Steam Awards and a THANK YOU!
notes.content:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/32463969/0e7f6d70e7c9ee829444876980fd6f948aa0b59c.gif[/img]

It's Steam Awards season, and there's no better time to sit back and look at the year we've had. Thanks to you, it's been an incredible one. We released the ONE LOVE DLC and announced our Switch version, which is all very exciting! 

Despite the cold, dark year that Brexit has had (honestly, not even WE could have predicted so many delays!) it's been a fantastic year for Not Tonight, so we're reaching out to give a big, heartfelt thank you! 

We had a fantastic time working on the ONE LOVE DLC, where we transported players to France and gave them a myriad of drinks to mix (snowflakes and backstops galore!) as well as some AMAZING dating partners (including, obviously, a dog) - we hope you all enjoyed it too!

Then we got to announce the very exciting SWITCH VERSION, which is a real blast to work on. We're confident we've got the control scheme down to something that feels natural (and a little bit rhythmical!) and the feedback we've gotten from taking it to PAX and EGX this year has been stellar! 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/32463969/6436871deb63b7e9bcbde873ae196d012c5d13f1.gif[/img]

The future of Not Tonight is very bright, and we cannot wait to share it all with you. Thank you so much for playing, for following our updates and for all your support for the last two years. 

Here's to a strong and stable future all round, 

Panic Barn & No More Robots 
xoxo

notes.title: BIG UPDATE: Soundtrack now available, new achievements, colorblind mode, and more!
notes.content:
Hey everyone,

big update today! Here's all the new stuff we've added:

[h1]The Not Tonight OST is now available![/h1]

We asked you lot to vote for your favourite 15 music tracks from the game... but then we decided to make the soundtrack 17 tracks long instead, because why not! That tracklist is as follows:

[b]Can You Feel Me (Chez Remix) - Love Beans
In the Blue - Tommy Ljungberg
Jack Elphick - Rough Diamond 1
Under the Stars - Squiid
Keep Coming Back to the Start - Martin Hall
Da Tooby - Down For the Long Run
Bless Up - Martin Landh
Mountain Downhill 3 - Niklas Gustavsson
Centipede - Ruzer
Name Tag - Nivicious
Believing in You (SLCT Remix) - Cacti
Copacabana - Onda Norte
Daxten - You Got Me
Don't Love You - Windshield
Differently - Sture Zetterberg
You Make me Feel - Staffan Carlen
I'll Be Good - Love Beans[/b]

You can grab the soundtrack from here: https://store.steampowered.com/app/954690/Not_Tonight_Original_Soundtrack/

[h1]New Achievements and Trading Cards![/h1]

Some people said they wished there were more achievements, signposting cool things and storylines you could find in the game. So we've added them! Boot the game up, and you'll see the full list -- good luck unlocking them all.

Oh, and we've added Steam Trading Cards and Emotes to the game as well, that you'll earn through simply playing the game. Enjoy!

[h1]Colorblind Mode[/h1]

For a while now the Not Tonight team has been looking for ways to ensure that all kinds of players can experience the game in all its glory. We've been speaking to a lot of players to make improvements, and the newest of these is our colour blind mode.

Having to distinguish between flags for some people is nearly impossible, and we felt just putting a filter over the screen wasn't an effective enough solution as it still meant that some players couldn't differentiate quickly between the countries of the Axis of Euro Evil and other, more acceptable countries at speed. We spoke to a wide range of players who shared their experiences and frustrations with us, and we took what we learned to make two distinct changes to the game for our colour blind mode.

[img]https://steamcdn-a.akamaihd.net/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/32463969/edd89b73bc2272e42e57edde4b39a78e4363dbe0.png[/img]

Firstly we've made IDs easier to read for various visual impairments by including a country code as part of the flag's design.  We've ensured that there are no busy backgrounds behind the lettering and that it is clear for people to read as part of each flag. If there's no code then the ID is clearly a fake (so kick 'em to the curb!).  Here's what some new IDs might look like to someone with colour blindness - 

The second change is that we've altered some visual cues for super-candy sales to shapes instead of colours. From here on out bubbles will still tell you who to sell a certain kind of super-candy to, but instead of needing to navigate blues and purples at speed, you'll now see triangles appear over the heads of people you should probably avoid selling to.

This along with the backwards hats and fake stripes mean that you never have to deal with colour when dealing.

[h1]Next up: Endless Mode and DLC![/h1]

We'll have new veeeeery soon about the upcoming Endless Mode, and some special story DLC, that will add a brand new chapter to the game.

Until then, enjoy the achievements, trading cards, and all the jazz!

Love the Not Tonight team xx

notes.title: Not Tonight imagines a drudge-filled Brexit dystopia
notes.content:
Not Tonight takes place in an alternative present. Britain's vote to leave the European Union has triggered a convulsion of xenophobia that sweeps a party called Britain Alone into power. Under their rule citizens who can't prove two generations of British citizenship are refused residency and forced to take temp gig economy jobs to make ends meet. As one such citizen, you sign up for infrequent bouncer work at a scuzzy local pub and spend your nights checking ID cards.

It plays like Papers, Please. You take the ID, check the picture, flag print, hologram, date-of-birth and the ID's expiry date and then either admit the guest or tell them to scram. The venue sets admission targets, but too many incorrect admissions will shut down the job early and pay nothing. Between gigs, which you sign up for via an app called BouncR, you sit in your hovel and take visits from neighbours and a corrupt policeman.

This bleak universe is rendered in very effective, grotty pixel art. There's an authentic caricature of a run down Somerset pub, complete with a ruined bus stop plastered in UKIP posters. As you take on new jobs you move into the cities and take jobs on tired old concrete high streets. The game's Brexit stance is the headline-grabber, but these sardonic snapshots of British nightlife are the best thing about the game. Queue-dodgers attempt to sneak in, telling you they know the owners. Angry clubbers get lairy with you for telling them they're underage, and it all happens to sound of muffled subterranean beats.

The moment-to-moment of the game is too gruelling in this beta version, though. The trouble with simulating a boring job is that it can make for a boring game. Papers, Please managed to put a lot of tactile interactions into the bureaucratic busywork to keep it involving, but Not Tonight doesn't manage this. The task of checking IDs gets extra layers when you're also checking a queue of VIPs against a checklist, but the sluggish progression means shifts are mind-numbing.

This might be intentional. The occasional attempts at humour fall flat for me, and it feels like a game that's trying to deliver a message rather than entertain. The Brexit stuff is a smokescreen, too. Not Tonight is really about a particular strain of British nationalism, and the fear of that moving from far right fringe groups into the mainstream. The way your character is referred to as a 'Euro' evokes the cadences of racist abuse commonly leveled at Pakistani communities just a few decades ago. It's got Brexit on the box, but it's about the Bradford riots, Windrush, and the UK's complicated relationship with immigration.

It's not a subtle parable and like a lot of worthy projects that come at you with a big message, it does end up feeling like taking medicine. As the player there's no room to come back and engage with the issues. Your character is monosyllabic and in the first few hours don't get to make many of the promised moral choices. The map suggests there will be a lot of venues to work at, but the idea of working all of those doors fills me with dread. Still, it's good to see a game at least to try to engage with some of these themes, even if the current state of the game could use improvement. The final version is due out this summer.

notes.title: Playing Not Tonight, a post-Brexit thriller
notes.content:
Not Tonight starts at the end, with the London Eye snapped and bobbing in the Thames, and political party Albion First in control. You are a bouncer taking tickets at the British Museum of History celebration party until - suddenly - it blows up. This is dystopian Britain; this is Brexit.

After the explosive beginning, Not Tonight rewinds. Your story begins in a rubbish-strewn hovel of a flat covered in xenophobic graffiti. You are a European housed and controlled by an oppressive government, and you must work to earn enough money to keep you from being deported.

Everything you do is monitored by the Nazi-like Albion First and embodied by Officer Jupp, your overseer. Your phone is issued by the party and the apps controlled by it, and the one you'll need most is BouncR, which offers you work.

notes.title: Not Tonight is a 'politically-charged satirical game' set in an alternate post-Brexit Britain
notes.content:
Besides the return of blue passports, what does the post-Brexit world hold for the United Kingdom? PanicBarn's Not Tonight portrays an an alternate Britain bursting with pixel art, satire plus RPG and management sim mechanics. 

Warning: The following trailer contains Nigel Farage:

Not Tonight is set in a Britain where Brexit talks have collapsed and a far-right government is in charge, so says publisher No More Robots. You assume control of 'Person of European Heritage #112' in Relocation Block B, whose kind have been rounded up and exiled. Forced out of your old life, you've landed a gig as a bouncer. "Work hard, stay out of trouble, and we might let you stay in the UK."

It all sounds pretty grim, set in a world that echoes Biff Tannen's alternate 1985 Hill Valley. Similar to the likes of Papers, Please, timed moral choices determine your approach—"Will you join the resistance and fight the regime, or keep your head down and hope that one day this will all be a distant memory?"—as you guard the doors of pubs, clubs, parties and festivals of your now dystopian city. 

"Upgrade your apartment, bouncer and equipment to better prepare yourself for the future," says the game's Steam page blurb. "Decide what lengths you'll go to in order to survive in a Britain on the verge of collapse."

Not Tonight is due on PC via Steam in "Summer 2018". Prospective players can sign up for the beta by joining the Not Tonight Discord.
